title: Cech cup products and pullback
statement: Let f:X' \to X be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], let U be an arbitrary open cover of X, and let U' be an open cover of X' together with a specified refinement map U' \to f^{-1}U in the sense of Stacks Tag 01FD. Let F and G be quasi-coherent modules on X [pqf-def-coherent], and write f^*F and f^*G for their pullbacks to X' [def-pc-module-pullback]. (a) The refinement cochain map from the Cech complex of (X,U,F) to that of (X',U',f^*F) is compatible with the usual pullback map H^p(X,F) \to H^p(X',f^*F) under the canonical maps from Cech cohomology to cohomology, \check H^p(U,F) \to H^p(X,F) and \check H^p(U',f^*F) \to H^p(X',f^*F), which exist for every open cover. (b) For an arbitrary open cover U of X, the signed Cech cup-product cochain map of Tag 07MB, Tot(Cech(U,F) \otimes Cech(U,G)) \to Cech(U,F\otimes G), induces on cohomology a map \check H^p(U,F) \otimes \check H^q(U,G) \to \check H^{p+q}(U,F\otimes G) that is compatible with the sheaf cup product H^p(X,F) \otimes H^q(X,G) \to H^{p+q}(X,F\otimes G) under the canonical maps \check H^n(U,-) \to H^n(X,-) (Stacks Tag 0FKV, cohomology-lemma-diagrams-commute); in particular, when these canonical maps are isomorphisms (for instance for a finite affine cover of a scheme with affine diagonal and quasi-coherent F, G), the Cech cup product is the sheaf cup product. Both assertions are natural in F,G and f.

source.place: Tags 01FD (cohomology-lemma-functoriality-cech), 07MB (cohomology-equation-needs-signs) and 0FKV (cohomology-lemma-diagrams-commute: the signed Cech cup product is compatible with the cup product on RGamma via the canonical maps, for every open covering)

proof.text: This is Stacks Tag 01FD (the item's own source) with f:X'\to X, the O_X-module F on the target, f^*F on the source, and the canonical f-map phi: f^*F \to f^*F (the identity). Choose c from the index set of U' to that of U with U'_a \subset f^{-1}(U_{c(a)}) and set gamma(s)_{a_0...a_p} = phi(s)_{c(a_0)...c(a_p)}, the restriction to U'_{a_0...a_p} of the pullback of s_{c(a_0)...c(a_p)}; pullback of sections commutes with restriction, so gamma is a cochain map. Choose injective resolutions F \to J^\bullet on X and f^*F \to I^\bullet on X', an injective resolution f_*I^\bullet \to J'^\bullet on X and a map beta: J^\bullet \to J'^\bullet over F \to f_*f^*F \to f_*I^\bullet (this choice defines the pullback map H^p(X,F) \to H^p(X',f^*F)). With the double complexes A^{p,q} = Cech^p(U',I^q), B^{p,q} = Cech^p(U,J^q), B'^{p,q} = Cech^p(U,J'^q), B''^{p,q} = Cech^p(U,f_*I^q), the rule defining gamma gives a map of double complexes B'' \to A, and the 01FD diagram (pentagon commuting by the choice of beta, the other squares by definition) commutes; going around it, inverting the quasi-isomorphisms Gamma(-,resolution) \to Tot, shows that the canonical maps of [lem-sc-cech-comparison-map-naturality] (defined from exactly these alpha and beta maps into Tot(A), Tot(B)) carry H^p(gamma) to the pullback map. This proves (a).

For the two Cech complexes and the sheaf tensor product, form the total tensor complex using d(a tensor b)=d(a) tensor b+(-1)^(deg a) a tensor d(b). The Cech cup map of Tag 07MB restricts the two factors to common intersections and inserts the total-complex signs; expanding the alternating restriction differential gives the Leibniz identity, with omitted-vertex terms cancelling in adjacent pairs. For sheaves in degree zero this specializes to the ordinary Cech cup product.

This is Stacks Tag 0FKV (the item's own source), applied to K = F and M = G placed in degree 0. Let A = Gamma(X,O_X). The sheaf cup product H^p(X,F) \otimes_A H^q(X,G) \to H^{p+q}(X,F \otimes G) is (Stacks section-cup-product) the map on cohomology of the composite R Gamma(X,F) \otimes_A^L R Gamma(X,G) --mu--> R Gamma(X, F \otimes^L_{O_X} G) \to R Gamma(X, F \otimes_{O_X} G), precomposed with H^p \otimes H^q \to H^{p+q} of the derived tensor, with the signs of the total tensor complex [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Tag 0FKV states that the square with top arrow Cech(U,F) \otimes_A^L Cech(U,G) \to R Gamma(X,F) \otimes_A^L R Gamma(X,G) (the canonical maps), left arrow Cech(U,F) \otimes^L \to Tot(Cech(U,F) \otimes_A Cech(U,G)) followed by the signed cup map of Step 2 (Tag 07MB) into Cech(U,F \otimes G), right arrow mu followed by R Gamma(X,F \otimes^L G) \to R Gamma(X,F \otimes G), and bottom arrow the canonical map Cech(U,F \otimes G) \to R Gamma(X,F \otimes G), commutes in D(A) for every open covering; its proof replaces F, G by Godement (flasque) resolutions, for which Gamma = Tot(Cech) = R Gamma, and reduces to the compatibility of the naive cup product with mu. For a single sheaf the canonical maps of the square are those of [lem-sc-cech-comparison-map-naturality] (both are induced by the Cech double complex of a resolution by Cech-acyclic sheaves). Taking H^p \otimes H^q \to H^{p+q} gives (b). No isomorphism of comparison maps is needed; when the canonical maps are isomorphisms the two cup products correspond, which is the 'in particular' clause.

The refinement map in Step 1 carries a cup cochain to the cup cochain of the pulled-back factors: on each intersection this is f^*(s tensor t)=f^*s tensor f^*t, and the total-complex sign depends only on the degrees. Thus the refinement square commutes with the cup map. Combining this identity with Step 3 proves compatibility of cup products with pullback. The same restriction and tensor identities commute with morphisms of F and G, and refinement functions compose, proving naturality.
